limitations: Fallback currently requires an empty standard ingress FIFO. The existing public API exposes remaining front bytes, not the original descriptor length/started state, so queued-prefix safety cannot be proved bridge-only. Nonempty FIFO is deliberately refused, including complete queued frames; this is more conservative than all-workload fallback.

Mission Planner continuous GCS traffic can keep a queue nonempty. A successful one-PARAM diagnostic run would not prove universal fallback under such backlog. Supporting proven unstarted queued prefixes requires separate introspection and tests.
The original R19 admission deadline still fails as designed; this change contains a safe pre-negotiation decline rather than accelerating a request whose fresh Grant is late.

Standard proxy fallback response/watchdog time is separate from the failed accelerated session. Original t0 remains recorded, and runner30-second measurement must not be reset or interpreted as fast-path success.
